html:
A former World Bank official chosen as prime minister by Benin's national conference of February 1990, who then defeated Mathieu Kerekou in the presidential election of March 1991.

The conference, of delegates from all parts of society, declared itself sovereign, and the army let it. It was one of the first times on the continent that a ruler lost power through such a process, and similar conferences followed in Togo, Mali, Congo and Niger. Soglo pushed economic reform but lost to Kerekou in 1996 and handed over power. Benin's peaceful changes made it a model, though its democracy has narrowed since the late 2010s. See also the end of the Cold War and African politics.
